biography: Alex Moore, born in the heart of Valencia, Spain, practically grew up on the scent of gasoline and burning rubber. His father, a mechanic for a local karting team, introduced him to the sport at a young age. Alex wasn't content just watching; at eight years old, he snuck out his father's tools and 'modified' his little sister's scooter into a makeshift racing machine. That earned him a stern talking-to, but also a go-kart for his ninth birthday. From regional karting championships to a surprising victory in a Formula 4 race at Jerez that caught the eye of a few independent teams, Alex has been on a rapid, if somewhat chaotic, ascent. Now, at 20, he's making a name for himself in the open-wheel racing world, showing flashes of brilliance hampered by his aggressive, sometimes reckless, approach.
drivingStyle: Moore's driving style is characterized by raw aggression and an almost reckless abandon. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and daring overtakes that often leave spectators gasping. While incredibly fast in short bursts, his tire management is frequently his Achilles' heel, and he can struggle to maintain consistent pace throughout an entire race distance. Pressure, however, seems to fuel him; the higher the stakes, the more fearless he becomes.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry sparked in their karting days, fueled by a controversial incident where Moore allegedly blocked Rossi in the final lap of a championship race, costing her the title.
A clash of styles – Tanaka's calculated precision versus Moore's raw aggression – often leads to tense battles on the track. Their contrasting personalities also contribute to the animosity.
Both are young, Spanish drivers vying for the same opportunities, leading to intense competition and occasional off-track sparring in the media.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristband given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Listens to a specific Spanish flamenco song at full volume in his headphones immediately before getting into the car.
Refuses to start a race weekend without first eating a plate of his mother's paella, no matter where in the world he is.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the limits until they scream."
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula 4 race at Jerez from a starting position of P15, showcasing his overtaking prowess and determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of a Formula 3 race in Barcelona due to excessive tire wear, costing him a likely victory.
